Whose money is it? How does a guy with whatever life story he felt he needed to front end load into your brain have that kicking around and decide to give it to you? Not that it couldn't make sense. Here is the thing. He doesn't sound like an experienced collaborator, one who is used to making money doing things with other people. Those folks behave differently. They tend to want to get to the point. They know they are never going to tell you everything and they certainly don't want to know everything about you: they would like to address the important things and get to the deal. If for some reason you ought to get $25k to also participate in what you both do, the other person would usually want to make sure earlier that you are for real and can work together. A lot of great people cannot work with other people.

In order to make your facts work, this person would have to be inexperienced enough at some key aspect to feel you are the key to success. That causes someone who has money for you to still need to tell you all about what they DO know to make up for what they need from you and still feel qualified to run with the big boys. The babble is making up for feeling inferior and wanting your approval. What strains credibility is that people who are falling over their feet to work with you do not usually have $25000 for "here you go, no strings, do your research."

Nevertheless, if you don't want to disappear into the mist for safety, the solution is the same for spook or rich, enthusiastic coauthor: have your smart friends check him out. Portrayal usually only works from one side. Other angles reveal what's going on. Get your Scaramucci on it.
